title: Forming the Harlem Hamfats and their personnel
summary: Morand formed the Hamfats with piano, E-flat clarinet, the McCoy brothers, drummers and a bassist. Only he and the bassist were from New Orleans, so playing New Orleans style was hard.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: Did you ever play any of those bands or did you form your own first?

Well, it's like I said, we got together and formed the Harlem Ampets. Well, who was in that group? Well, myself on trumpet, little Horace Malcolm, Horace Malcolm on piano, Odell Rand on clarinet. He played an E-flat clarinet. He was a little short fellow with a little short clarinet. And Joe McCoy on guitar. His brother Charlie McCoy, he played a mandolin. Mandolin on guitar, whatever you call it. I think it's, it's 12 strings on it. He played a band. We had different drummers. P.C. Williams was one. And John Alenji on bass.
Were those all New Orleans men or were there many from Chicago?
No, just John Alenji and myself.
He was the only New Orleans men on the Harlem Ampets. Did they play New Orleans style or?
Well, I tried to get them to play New Orleans style, but it's a kind of hard proposition. Well, how did you? Playing New Orleans style, you'd have to be born here tonight.
